candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Genesis
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Genesis, Section XLI.38. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13, ed. J. Gwynn / Schaff (1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Genesis (c. 360 AD)

'And Pharaoh said unto his servants, Can we find such a one as this is, a man in whom the Spirit of God is?' Ephrem reads Pharaoh's recognition as a striking example: a pagan king discerns the Spirit of God in a Hebrew slave. Tewahedo missiological theology preserves this verse as the canonical warrant for the principle that divine presence can be recognised by those outside the covenant — implicit support for the Tewahedo openness to natural-revelation theology.
